ep4_pioneer2.name: Pioneer 2
ep4_pioneer2.era: A.U.W. 3086, the first days after the meteor fell, as hunters are first sent down to the Crater
ep4_pioneer2.summary: Pioneer 2 still orbits Ragol, its people waiting to settle, when a meteor the Lab said would miss is knocked onto the planet by a beam from the surface. The news says there is nothing to worry about, but the ship shook, soldiers are busy, the Principal's research team is missing and the Guild's board is filling with Crater work.
known_facts: In A.U.W. 3086 Pioneer 2 still orbits Ragol, and its people expected the work of settling the planet to go ahead at last.
Ship watchers tracked an ordinary meteor that the Lab calculated would miss both Ragol and the ship, so no announcement was made.
A single beam of light shot up from Ragol's surface and knocked the meteor onto the planet; no one can say what fired it.
The shockwave was felt aboard, but neither Pioneer 2 nor the Central Dome was harmed.
The meteor left a huge crater with a strange light shining inside, and ferocious creatures are swarming out around it.
The official news says the meteor is nothing to worry about, while town gossip claims it grazed Pioneer 2 and caused the shaking.
Some residents took the shaking for the end of the world.
The Principal's own research team went down to the Crater and never checked in, and skilled hunters are being sent to find it.
Uniformed soldiers have been frantically busy since the impact, some say since a little before it.
A guard admits the troops cannot deploy for reasons he calls internal, and a soldier says the army lacks the manpower to survive as it is.
The Hunter's Guild board is filling with Crater jobs from clients who give no names and want no questions asked.
Civilians still cannot go down to Ragol.
open_mysteries: What fired the beam of light from Ragol's surface?
Why did the meteor hit Ragol when every calculation said it would miss?
Why were the soldiers busy even before the impact, and why can the troops not deploy?
What happened to the Principal's missing research team?
Is the meteor really nothing to worry about?
hidden_truths: Leo Grahart, former captain of the military's WORKS division, brought the meteor down on purpose; the beam's exact source was never confirmed.
The meteor carries the D-factor, a Photon-like energy drawn from Dark Falz's own cells, and it lies behind the new creatures.
WORKS was already running secret operations at the impact site, hidden even from the Principal and the Lab.
A girl who spends her time at the Medical Center, Rupika, is a Neo-Newman carrying the D-factor, secretly under the Principal's protection, and WORKS will kidnap her.
A conspiracy hides behind the Pioneer Project itself: the military's MOTHER Project, which Leo means to revive.
Black Paper, the government's own covert arm, is secretly at work on Ragol against WORKS, recovering Pioneer 1's research data.

job_hooks: Train up to the level the Principal's office wants before it sends more skilled hunters to the Crater.
Build a stake of Meseta for an informant who sells what he hears only at a steep price.
Gather Photon Drops or other materials for a collector who trades them for news.
Prove yourself to a client picking an elite team for a quiet job below.
Put in long hours on standby while the Guild and the Principal call up great numbers of hunters.
Help a short-handed army with work it lacks the manpower to do.
Earn the trust of a Guild client who gives no name and wants no questions asked.
avoid: Never say who or what fired the beam; at this moment no one knows.
Never name WORKS, Leo Grahart or Black Paper as behind the meteor or the Crater; no one aboard knows yet.
Never link the meteor to the D-factor, MOTHER, the Heaven Striker, the HS Project or Dark Falz.
Never mention a missing girl or Rupika; she has not vanished yet, and her secret is the heart of the episode.
Pioneer 2 and the Central Dome were not damaged; the meteor grazing the ship is only a rumour.
Pioneer 2 is still in orbit and settlement has not begun; civilian clients never go down to Ragol themselves.
Never have the Principal's missing research team turn up; there was no trace of it.
Call him the Principal or Principal Tyrell, not the Governor.

ep4_crater.name: Crater
ep4_crater.era: A.U.W. 3086, the first days after the impact, when the Principal's research team has gone missing in the Crater
ep4_crater.summary: A huge crater, glowing with a strange light from inside, where a meteor struck Ragol after a mysterious beam knocked it off course. The devastated wasteland around it swarms with ferocious new creatures, and four routes lead in toward the central Crater and its interior. The Principal's research team went down and never checked in, and hunters are now being sent after it.
known_facts: A meteor fell on Ragol after a single beam of light from the surface knocked it off an orbit the Lab had said would miss.
Where it struck lies a huge crater with a strange light shining from inside.
The devastated wasteland around the impact swarms with ferocious new creatures, and great numbers of hunters are being sent down to subdue them.
Four routes, from the east, west, south and north, lead toward the central Crater and the impact site.
The Principal's own research team went down to the Crater and never checked in.
The Principal's office is sending skilled hunters after the team, with the teleporter set to its coordinates, and Irene warns the risk is enormous.
Crater creatures attack in packs; veterans advise watching the radar and never getting surrounded.
Guns barely hurt Yowies and Satellite Lizards from the front, so hunters aim for backs and sides; Techniques and blades work from any angle.
Guild clients who give no names post Crater outbreak jobs and tell hunters not to ask questions or go nosing around.
Uniformed soldiers have been frantically busy since the impact, some say since a little before it.
open_mysteries: What fired the beam that knocked the meteor off course?
Why did the meteor hit Ragol when every calculation said it would miss?
What happened to the Principal's research team?
What is the strange light inside the Crater?
Where did so many new creatures come from so suddenly?
Why were the soldiers busy even before the impact?
hidden_truths: Leo Grahart, former captain of the military's WORKS division, brought the meteor down on purpose; the beam's exact source was never confirmed.
The meteor carries the D-factor, a Photon-like energy drawn from Dark Falz's own cells, and it lies behind the new creatures.
WORKS is already operating in the Crater in secret and will blockade the western, eastern and southern routes in turn.
Fissures in the Crater's floor open onto layered strata and a vast Subterranean Desert below.
Leo Grahart will take a newman girl, Rupika, down beneath the Crater to use her D-factor power for his project.
The Lab already holds research data on the Crater's interior, and someone will tamper with its files before hunters recover them.

ep4_desert.name: Subterranean Desert
ep4_desert.era: A.U.W. 3086, when hunters are first teleported into the upper layer of the Subterranean Desert beneath the Crater
ep4_desert.summary: Beneath the Crater's strata lies the Subterranean Desert, a labyrinth of caverns and open spaces running ever deeper, so strange that some wonder whether it is natural or made. Hunters are now teleported into its upper layer while savage creatures fill the hospital, the military pursues unexplained plans, and rumour says several groups are racing to find a missing girl. Hunters who reach the deepest desert tell of three giant segmented serpents: Saint-Milion, Shambertin and Kondrieu.
known_facts: Fissures in the Crater's floor open onto layered strata, and beneath them lies the Subterranean Desert.
The desert is a labyrinth of caverns and open spaces running deeper and deeper, and the teleporter can now reach its upper layer.
The Principal's office warns that the desert is a maze, its creatures are savage, and the hospital is already full.
New creatures teem at every level, among them shadowy, long-clawed things shaped almost like people.
The military has some unexplained plan to thin out the desert's creatures.
The military has blockaded the Crater's western, eastern and southern routes and orders hunters out of its territory.
WORKS, once a powerful homeworld special operations force, is active below, and its soldiers argue among themselves about their captain.
WORKS and the Hunter's Guild dislike each other, and a secret counter-force against WORKS is rumoured to be very active.
The Principal's office complains that the military hides its activities and keeps blocking its search teams.
Town talk says a strange girl who used to spend time at the Medical Center is missing, and hunters from three powerful organisations are racing to find her.
The Lab turned out to hold research data on the Crater's interior, though nobody knows what it was studying.
Hunters who reach the deepest desert tell of giant segmented serpents in three colours, rarely met: Saint-Milion, Shambertin and Kondrieu.
open_mysteries: Is the Subterranean Desert natural, or was it made?
Is the meteor behind the savage new creatures?
What are the giant serpents of the deepest desert?
Where is the missing girl, and why are so many groups racing to find her?
What is WORKS doing below, and what is the military's plan for the creatures?
Who is the secret counter-force working against WORKS?
hidden_truths: The meteor carries the D-factor, a Photon-like energy drawn from Dark Falz's own cells, and it lies behind the creatures.
The desert's shadowy, long-clawed humanoids are of Dark Falz's own family.
A thought-entity sleeping in the meteor waits at the desert's bottom and goes berserk; people later speak of a huge creature born of the D-factor.
Rupika is a Neo-Newman with the D-factor in her DNA; Leo Grahart of WORKS kidnapped her to revive the MOTHER Project and power his father's Heaven Striker.
Leo Grahart brought the meteor down on purpose to harness its D-factor energy, which only Rupika can control.
The counter-force against WORKS is Black Paper, the government's own covert arm; Sue, and most likely Kireek, work for it.

examples.brief: In the first days after the impact, a commander who never gave a name hired a team of elite hunters for a secret operation at the impact site, now overrun with gigantic monsters. Neither the Principal nor the Lab was to know, so the team had to get in and out unnoticed. The reward was 10,000 Meseta, and silence.

The Principal's own research team went down to the Crater and never checked in. Irene went over the meteor's fall, set the teleporter to the team's last coordinates and sent the hunter to find them, warning plainly that the risk was enormous.

A Lab team was ambushed in the Crater and lost its research data. Irene hired hunters to recover it along the western route, working with the other hunters on the job; rescuing researchers was welcome, but the data came first.
On one of the Crater's routes, a collector asked the hunter for four Photon Drops, offering in return to share what he had heard about the trouble below.

Clients who would say nothing about themselves posted Guild jobs to wipe out creature outbreaks level by level through the Subterranean Desert, calling it a test of limits. They told hunters not to ask questions or go nosing around.

The Principal's office wanted a large meteor fragment brought back for the Lab to analyse, hoping to learn what lay behind the creatures. Irene warned that no one had yet returned with one, and that the deepest desert was said to be a living hell.
